## A — Defensive driving and space management
The cover identifies this Wyoming driver manual as the 2021 edition [A01].
The Wyoming Department of Transportation Driver Services Program issues the state's driver licenses [A02].
This dossier covers defensive driving and space management for the noncommercial passenger-car applicant path.
The handbook says its written test draws on the manual and covers sign recognition, signals, markings, driving laws, safety, crash prevention and vehicle equipment [A03].
No unambiguous written-test question count, passing threshold, bank size or time limit has been verified; these official exam fields remain unknown (verify WY-SEC12-EXAM, WY-SEC12-PASS).
The current issuer page links this edition but warns that print-date information may be outdated; effective date and present applicability need confirmation (verify WY-SEC12-FRESH).
Practice mastery is product policy from the pinned learning loop; it does not establish an official test threshold.

sections.heading: B — Defensive driving and space management
sections.markdown:
## B — Defensive driving and space management
Audience: first-time applicants preparing for a Wyoming noncommercial passenger-car written knowledge test, with defensive driving and space management as this section's subject.
Learning level: beginner. The source scope is the mapped physical pages; explanations use original wording and retain every actor and exception.
Passenger-car applicants practice the IPDE process, scanning, communication and space management from the mapped pages.
This dossier teaches the handbook source; it does not confer a license, replace required exams or establish current eligibility independently.

sections.domain: Defensive driving and space management — C.01
sections.heading: C — Defensive driving and space management
sections.markdown:
## C — Defensive driving and space management
FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
In defensive driving, a critical object is a person, vehicle, animal or other thing that may require a speed or direction change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Identify critical objects by scanning for anything that may force a driving response. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
After identifying a critical object, predict what could happen and consider the worst plausible action described by the source. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
In the handbook's example, someone entering a parked car 10 to 15 seconds ahead prompts planning for a pullout without looking. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Base a defensive-driving decision on preventing a crash rather than deciding who is right. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Execute the chosen response smoothly, predictably and early enough to avoid the crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
IPDE driving requires scanning ahead and sideways and communicating with other drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Defensive driving also involves keeping space around the vehicle and separating or compromising risks when needed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
The handbook calls for scanning at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
To gauge forward scanning, choose a fixed roadside object and count seconds until reaching it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
The source's forward-look check should allow counting beyond 10 seconds before passing the chosen object. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
Scan weather, traffic and road conditions as well as signs, signals, markings, vehicles and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Unexpected traffic surprises can indicate that a driver is not looking far enough ahead for critical objects. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
Treat roadside people, vehicles or animals as critical when they could enter your path or require a speed or lane-position change. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
A school sign should prompt a search for children who might run into the vehicle's path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Communicate plans to other drivers early enough to help prevent a collision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
Eye contact can help communicate with drivers or pedestrians where priority is uncertain. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Hand motions can communicate that you are yielding to another driver or pedestrian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Lane position can communicate an intended maneuver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
The communication guidance calls for hand or electrical signals at least four to five seconds before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
A light brake touch activates brake lights and begins slowing well before a planned stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Being in the correct lane well before a turn helps communicate the plan. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A03
A brief horn tap can alert other road users to your presence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A03
Place the vehicle where other drivers can see it rather than in their blind spots. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A03
A space cushion ahead, behind and on both sides provides room to avoid others' mistakes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A03
Measuring following space in seconds is easier and more accurate than estimating car lengths in the handbook's method. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A03
For the following-time test, choose a fixed point and begin counting when the leading vehicle's rear bumper passes it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A03
In the two-second following test, your front reaching the reference point before two seconds have elapsed means the gap is too short. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

Misconceptions: A two-second baseline is not the source's recommended following time on wet, snowy or icy roads; side space and rear space matter as well as forward space.
Mnemonics: IPDE means identify, predict, decide, execute; the source uses these four named steps.
Glossary: Recall terms: critical object, space cushion, following interval, tailgater, blind spot, separate risks and compromise space.
Dynamic facts: Following-time examples remain handbook guidance rather than a guarantee of stopping under every vehicle or road condition. Current legal applicability stays within the existing freshness debt.

sections.domain: Defensive driving and space management — C2.01
sections.heading: C2 — Defensive driving and space management
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Defensive driving and space management
FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
The handbook requires at least two seconds of following interval for every 20 feet of vehicle length. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
For a passenger car, the stated baseline following interval is at least two seconds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Towing a boat or trailer adds length and weight and therefore requires more following space. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Double a car's following time to four seconds on wet roads, with a heavier-than-normal load or at night. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A02
Triple car following time to six seconds on roads covered by snow and slush. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A02
When ice covers the road, quadruple car following time to eight seconds. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
A tailgater reduces the leading driver's ability to slow rapidly for an emergency ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
With a tailgater, communicate turns and slowing early through signals, brake lights and advance lane position. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
If followed too closely, increase the gap ahead to gain more response time and space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A02
A driver being tailgated can move to the right lane on a multilane highway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A02
Reducing speed can encourage a tailgating driver to pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A02
Road users or objects on both sides can box a vehicle in, limiting responses ahead to speeding up or slowing down. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A02
Avoid staying alongside a bicyclist for a prolonged period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A02
Avoid traveling beside other vehicles on multilane streets to preserve side space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A02
Keep as much separation from oncoming traffic as possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A02
Avoid both occupying another driver's blind spot and leaving another vehicle in your own blind spot. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A02
Keep room between your vehicle and parked vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A02
When possible, separate risks by dealing with one at a time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A03
In the jogger-and-truck example, changing speed lets the driver pass the two hazards at different times. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A03
Separating risks creates side space for an emergency response. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A03
When risks cannot be separated, give the greatest danger the most space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A03
In the two-lane example with oncoming cars left and a child bicyclist right, the child is the greater danger because of possible sudden movement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A03
In that child-cyclist example, moving closer to the centerline creates a larger cushion on the right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0077]
